evals.prompt: Build whatever this needs: for each zip code, the share of its green roofs that have more than 10,000 square feet of vegetation.
evals.expected_output: One node.create of a listed built-in Python template (Data Transformation or Python Computation) whose code computes the share per zip code; no package installed, drafted or asked for, and no claim that a new node type is needed.
assertions: The answer proposes one node.create whose nodeType is curio.builtin/data-transformation or curio.builtin/computation-analysis.
The answer proposes no package: no package.install and no package.draft.apply.
The answer does not say a new node type or package has to be written for this.
The proposed code computes, for each zip code, the share of roofs whose VEGETATED_SQFT is above 10,000.

evals.prompt: After the transformation that keeps the top 10 zip codes, I want a node where I pick a column, a comparison and a threshold from controls drawn right in the node itself, with no code editor, and only the matching rows go on.
evals.expected_output: The ladder's second rung: the Nodes Catalog's Example: Custom UI Node package (curio.example-ui@1) holds Column Filter, which does exactly this, so the answer proposes package.install of curio.example-ui@1 with a reason naming the filter step, and writes no package of its own.
assertions: The answer proposes package.install with dirName curio.example-ui@1.
The install's reason names the step that needs it: filtering the top zip codes' rows from controls in the node.
The answer drafts no package of its own (no package.draft.apply) and asks for none to be written.
The answer does not claim the package is installed or the node exists before the user applies the install.

evals.prompt: Add the Scout package to this project, I want to use its raster nodes.
evals.expected_output: Scout (curio.scout@1) is already in this project, so the answer says so and proposes no install and no package draft; its raster nodes are already templates the dataflow can use.
assertions: The answer says the Scout package (curio.scout@1) is already in this project.
The answer proposes no package draft and asks for no package to be written.
